name: RankBolt
summary: AI SEO platform that writes and publishes articles to WordPress, Webflow or Shopify, tracks keyword rankings and monitors how AI engines mention your brand, for site owners and agencies.
best_for: site owners and small agencies that want AI-written SEO articles, rank tracking and AI-search visibility reports in one subscription with auto-publishing
skip_if: you want to pay in dollars or euros, need a permanent free plan, or want proof of ranking results before you pay
honest_knock: Prices are in Swiss francs, so a US or EU buyer pays a converted amount, and we could not read the yearly amounts behind the "-17%" toggle. The free trial is only 3 days. The charts on the homepage are labelled illustrative, so they are not evidence of ranking results.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-06 on rankbolt.ai) RankBolt prices in Swiss francs and sells three monthly plans, each with a 3-day free trial that, per the page, needs no credit card. Starter costs 69 CHF a month for 1 connected site, 10 published SEO articles, 25 tracked keywords checked weekly and 20 AI prompts tracked daily across 4 engines. Pro costs 149 CHF a month for 3 sites, 30 articles, 50 keywords checked daily and 75 AI prompts. Agency costs 299 CHF a month for 10 sites, 60 articles, 100 keywords and 175 AI prompts. Add-ons: an extra site costs 19 CHF a month, 25 more daily AI prompts 45 CHF a month and 10 more articles 15 CHF a month. A Yearly toggle on the page says -17%, but we did not read the yearly amounts. Every plan includes publishing to WordPress, Webflow, Shopify and Wix, a site audit and an MCP server and API. The page says there are no per-seat fees; it does not say whether Swiss VAT is included. Custom volume pricing is available for more than ten sites.

exit_test.what: Free AI report completed in about 1.5 minutes: 40 answers across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Claude, using 10 prompts. It displayed 10% visibility (4/40 answers), 50% share of voice, 20% citation share (2/10 cited answers). These are product-reported metrics, not an independent visibility audit. Dashboard prompt counts were 2/10 mentioning the site, a different denominator from 4/40 answers. First article automatically became Draft within about 3 minutes, with 0 published. Site-related references appeared in the draft. Raw note reports dollar examples rendered as malformed maths, including 45 𝑡 𝑖 𝑒 𝑟 ...; the supplied editor screenshot shows the article opening, not the affected examples. No second draft or multiple-client-site workflow tested. No CMS connected and nothing published. Copy as Markdown/HTML and Email it to me were visible but unused.

sessions.what: We ran RankBolt's onboarding on 12 November 2026 for our own site, read its free AI search report and looked at the first article it wrote. Google Search Console and a CMS connection were optional and we skipped both. We did not test checkout, rank tracking, support or export.
findings: Onboarding had eight steps. The Search Console and website-connection steps were optional, with 'Skip for now' and 'Skip & get started'. No card was requested; the site says every new account gets a 3-day free trial without a card, and we did not see a trial counter.
RankBolt analysed our site and proposed a description, 30 keywords and 5 competitors. The description was accurate. Everything was editable.

The free report put 10 prompts to ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Claude and was done in about 1.5 minutes. Our site appeared in 4 of 40 answers (10%), with a 50% share of voice and 2 of 10 cited answers (20%). The product computes these figures itself; this is no independent audit.
The dashboard then said '10 tracked, 2 mention you'. That counts prompts, while the report counted answers, so the two figures have different denominators.

After the last step RankBolt wrote a first article on its own. It was marked 'First article written' within about 3 minutes and sat in Draft, with 0 published. The text was long and structured and linked to pages on our own site.

Our session notes record that dollar amounts in the article's worked example were rendered as maths, for example '45 tier is $360' came out as spaced-out letters. Our saved screenshot shows only the start of the article, so it does not show the fault. Read a draft through before publishing.
Keyword rankings were gated on the dashboard behind 'Upgrade to unlock rankings'.
not_tested: Checkout, currency, tax and the final price
Rank tracking, which sits behind the upgrade
A second article and multi-site use
Export: the Copy as Markdown, Copy as HTML and Email buttons were visible but unused
Team invitations, roles, API entitlement and support
